positioning: A small white terrier with a big opinion of itself.
story: The West Highland White Terrier is the size of a loaf of bread and the attitude of a mountain. It carries itself like a general and digs like a gold miner.
The breed comes from the West Highlands of Scotland. Farmers kept sturdy little terriers to hunt rats, foxes, and badgers among the rocks. The best ones worked underground, and they needed courage.

A famous story says Colonel Malcolm of Poltalloch mistook one of his red terriers for a fox and shot it by accident. He then bred white dogs so nobody would make the mistake again. Whether true or not, the dogs stayed white.
The AKC recognized the breed in 1908. Today the Westie is a TV star, a dog food mascot, and one of the best-loved small dogs in America.
At home, a Westie is bold, cheerful, and busy. It digs, it barks, and it assumes the household needs its supervision. It will play fetch until you drop.
Give it a fenced yard, a brush, and a sense of humor. A Westie will supply the rest.
rank_cap: The small white terrier of Scotland (AKC)
fblocks: Named for the West Highlands of Scotland. The earlier name was the Poltalloch Terrier, after the Malcolm family estate.
Cesar, the dog food mascot. A Westie also trots across the label of a famous Scotch whisky.
Digs, barks, and chases. Skin allergies are common. A hand-stripped coat keeps the texture right.
A harsh white outer coat over a soft undercoat. Black nose, dark eyes, and a carrot-shaped tail.
Fifteen to twenty pounds. Ten to eleven inches tall. Recognized by the AKC in 1908.
days: Old Mac naps on a plaid blanket on a hay bale. The pumpkins keep watch.
World Animal Day. The Westie began as a Scottish rat catcher in the rocks.
A Scottish colonel bred white terriers so he would never mistake one for a fox.
Two Westies ride a wagon full of pumpkins. They think they are the harvest.
A carved smile greets Poppy. She stares it down. Meet the world head on.
A pumpkin vine makes a fine scarf. Angus has decided on the look.
Puppies tumble in the hay among tiny pumpkins. No rules apply.
last_walk:
The jack-o’-lanterns flicker, and the sky goes violet.
Angus and Poppy leave the glowing patch together. Their white coats catch every ember of light. A Westie leaves a party only when it has seen all of it. Tonight, they have seen enough.
